title: Prakrama 4, Sarga 11. Hearing of the Pastimes Beginning with Akrura's Coming
html:
Krishnadasa tells of the manifest pastimes: Akrura comes to Vraja for Rama and Krishna; Yashoda despairs and her sons console her; the gopis fall into divine madness, yet each sees her own Lord at her side; Rama and Krishna leave for Mathura with Akrura; Akrura's vision in the Yamuna, the washerman, Sudaman, Kubja, the broken bow, the night on Nanda's lap; listening, the Lord is filled with each of these moods

Verse 1

एवं स नित्यलीलाभिर्दीव्यति व्रजभूमिषु।
प्रकटानुमतेनापि कथ्यते यत्तथा शृणु॥१॥

evaṁ sa nityalīlābhirdīvyati vrajabhūmiṣu|
prakaṭānumatenāpi kathyate yattathā śṛṇu||1||

evam — thus; sah — He; nitya-lilabhih — with eternal pastimes; divyati — sports; vraja-bhumishu — in the lands of Vraja; prakata-anumatena — according to (the view of) the manifest pastimes; api — also; kathyate — is told; yat — what; tatha — likewise; shrinu — hear.

1"Thus He sports in the lands of Vraja with His eternal pastimes. But hear also what is told according to the manifest pastimes1.

Verse 2

कंसेन प्रहितोऽक्रूरो रथेनागतवान् पथि।
स्मरन् श्रीरामकृष्णौ च तयोर्दर्शनलालसः॥२॥

kaṁsena prahito'krūro rathenāgatavān pathi|
smaran śrīrāmakṛṣṇau ca tayordarśanalālasaḥ||2||

kamsena — by Kamsa; prahitah — sent; akrurah — Akrura; rathena — by chariot; agatavan — came; pathi — on the road; smaran — remembering; shri-rama-krishnau — Sri Rama and Krishna; cha — and; tayoh — Them; darshana-lalasah — longing to see.

2Sent by Kamsa, Akrura came by chariot; on the way he remembered Sri Rama and Krishna, longing to see Them,

Verse 3

नानामनोरथैः पूर्णः प्रेमाश्रुपुलकैर्वृतः।
ददर्श चरणाम्भोजचिह्नमत्रैव पावनम्॥३॥

nānāmanorathaiḥ pūrṇaḥ premāśrupulakairvṛtaḥ|
dadarśa caraṇāmbhojacihnamatraiva pāvanam||3||

nana-manorathaih — with various longings; purnah — filled; prema-ashru-pulakaih — with tears of love and thrills; vritah — covered; dadarsha — saw; charana-ambhoja-chihnam — the marks of the lotus feet; atra — here; eva — very; pavanam — purifying.

3filled with many hopes, covered with tears of love and thrills of joy. And here he saw the purifying marks of Their lotus feet2.

Verse 4

रथादुत्थाय शिरसि धूलिमादाय सत्वरम्।
दण्डवत् पतितो भूमौ दृष्ट्वा श्रीरामकेशवौ॥४॥

rathādutthāya śirasi dhūlimādāya satvaram|
daṇḍavat patito bhūmau dṛṣṭvā śrīrāmakeśavau||4||

rathat — from the chariot; utthaya — rising; shirasi — on his head; dhulim — dust; adaya — taking; satvaram — hastily; dandavat — like a rod; patitah — fell; bhumau — to the ground; drishtva — seeing; shri-rama-keshavau — Sri Rama and Keshava.

4Seeing Sri Rama and Keshava, he hastily got down from the chariot, placed dust on his head and fell to the ground, stretched out like a rod.

Verse 5

आभ्यां सम्मानितो नीतः स्वगृहं परमादरात्।
पूजितः स्वन्नपानाद्यैर्नन्देन सुमहात्मना॥५॥

ābhyāṁ sammānito nītaḥ svagṛhaṁ paramādarāt|
pūjitaḥ svannapānādyairnandena sumahātmanā||5||

abhyam — by the two; sammanitah — honoured; nitah — was led; sva-griham — to their home; parama-adarat — with great respect; pujitah — was entertained; su-anna-pana-adyaih — with fine food, drink and the rest; nandena — by Nanda; su-maha-atmana — most noble-hearted.

5They honoured him and led him with great respect to Their home, and the noble-hearted Nanda regaled him with fine food, drink and all the rest.

Verse 6

कंसचिकीर्षितं श्रुत्वा रामकृष्णसमन्वितः।
नन्द आघोषयद् गोष्ठं मथुरागमनाय च॥६॥

kaṁsacikīrṣitaṁ śrutvā rāmakṛṣṇasamanvitaḥ|
nanda āghoṣayad goṣṭhaṁ mathurāgamanāya ca||6||

kamsa-chikirshitam — Kamsa's intention; shrutva — hearing; rama-krishna-samanvitah — together with Rama and Krishna; nandah — Nanda; aghoshayat — proclaimed to; goshtham — the cowherd village; mathura-gamanaya — the journey to Mathura; cha — and.

6Hearing of Kamsa's intention, Nanda, together with Rama and Krishna, proclaimed to the cowherd village the journey to Mathura3.

Verse 7–8

एवं श्रुत्वा परमसुखदौ रामकृष्णौ ददर्श च।
वात्सल्ये सारभूता सा यशोदा रामकृष्णयोः।
करं धृत्वा क्रोडीकृत्य बभाषे सत्वरं हरिम्॥७-८॥

evaṁ śrutvā paramasukhadau rāmakṛṣṇau dadarśa ca|
vātsalye sārabhūtā sā yaśodā rāmakṛṣṇayoḥ|
karaṁ dhṛtvā kroḍīkṛtya babhāṣe satvaraṁ harim||7-8||

evam — this; shrutva — hearing; parama-sukha-dau — the givers of the highest joy; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; dadarsha — she saw; cha — and; vatsalye — in parental love; sara-bhuta — the very essence; sa — she; yashoda — Yashoda; rama-krishnayoh — for Rama and Krishna; karam — the hand; dhritva — taking; krodikritya — taking onto her lap; babhashe — spoke; satvaram — hurriedly; harim — to Hari.

7–8Hearing this, Yashoda — the very essence of parental love for Rama and Krishna — looked upon her sons, the givers of the highest joy, took Them by the hand, drew them onto her lap and hurriedly said to Hari:

Verse 9

ततः किं मां परित्यज्य मथुरां गन्तुमिच्छथः।
न दृष्ट्वा मुखचन्द्रं वां कथं धास्यामि जीवितम्॥९॥

tataḥ kiṁ māṁ parityajya mathurāṁ gantumicchathaḥ|
na dṛṣṭvā mukhacandraṁ vāṁ kathaṁ dhāsyāmi jīvitam||9||

tatah — so; kim — is it that; mam — me; parityajya — abandoning; mathuram — to Mathura; gantum — to go; icchathah — you two wish; na — not; drishtva — seeing; mukha-chandram — the moon of the faces; vam — of you two; katham — how; dhasyami — shall I keep; jivitam — life.

9'So will You two abandon me and go off to Mathura? How shall I keep my life if I do not see the moon of Your faces?'

Verse 10

नहि नहीति मातस्त्वत्सन्निधिं क्रोडमास्थितौ।
तिष्ठावस्त्वं विजानीयाः सत्यं सत्यं न संशयः॥१०॥

nahi nahīti mātastvatsannidhiṁ kroḍamāsthitau|
tiṣṭhāvastvaṁ vijānīyāḥ satyaṁ satyaṁ na saṁśayaḥ||10||

na hi na hi — no, no; iti — thus; matah — O mother; tvat-sannidhim — near you; krodam — in your lap; asthitau — abiding; tishthavah — we two remain; tvam — you; vijaniyah — should know; satyam satyam — truly, truly; na — no; samshayah — doubt.

10'No, no, Mother — we shall stay close to you, in your lap. Know that this is true, true, without a doubt.'

Verse 11

श्रुत्वा प्रेमपरीतात्मा चुम्बमाना मुखं तयोः।
स्थिरीभूत्वा सुखं मेने रामकृष्णौ हृदि स्थितौ॥११॥

śrutvā premaparītātmā cumbamānā mukhaṁ tayoḥ|
sthirībhūtvā sukhaṁ mene rāmakṛṣṇau hṛdi sthitau||11||

shrutva — hearing; prema-parita-atma — her heart overwhelmed with love; chumbamana — kissing; mukham — the faces; tayoh — of the two; sthiri-bhutva — growing calm; sukham — happiness; mene — she felt; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; hridi — in her heart; sthitau — abide.

11Hearing this, she, overwhelmed with love, kissed Their faces; then she grew calm and felt happiness: Rama and Krishna abide in her heart.

Verse 12

एतन्मध्ये परमविवशा दुःखसन्तप्तचित्ता
शून्यं मत्वा सकलभुवनं दासिकाः पृच्छमाना।
कोऽसौ दूरात् शमनसदृश आगतो राजदूतो
नन्दद्वारि सकलव्रजजनप्राणसंबाधकारी॥१२॥

etanmadhye paramavivaśā duḥkhasantaptacittā
śūnyaṁ matvā sakalabhuvanaṁ dāsikāḥ pṛcchamānā|
ko'sau dūrāt śamanasadṛśa āgato rājadūto
nandadvāri sakalavrajajanaprāṇasaṁbādhakārī||12||

etan-madhye — meanwhile; parama-vivasha — utterly helpless; duhkha-santapta-chitta — her heart burning with grief; shunyam — empty; matva — deeming; sakala-bhuvanam — the whole world; dasikah — her maids; pricchamana — asking; kah — who; asau — this; durat — from afar; shamana-sadrishah — like Shamana (Yama); agatah — come; raja-dutah — king's messenger; nanda-dvari — at Nanda's door; sakala-vraja-jana-prana-sambadha-kari — who torments the life of all the people of Vraja.

12But meanwhile, utterly helpless, her heart burning with grief, she deemed the whole world empty and kept asking her maids, 'Who is this king's messenger, like Yama4, who has come from afar to Nanda's door — he who torments the life of all the people of Vraja?'

Verse 13

श्रुत्वा व्रजस्त्रियः सर्वा रामकृष्णात्मकेहया।
नानाभावैरुपेतास्ता दिव्योन्मादसुलक्षणाः॥१३॥

śrutvā vrajastriyaḥ sarvā rāmakṛṣṇātmakehayā|
nānābhāvairupetāstā divyonmādasulakṣaṇāḥ||13||

shrutva — hearing; vraja-striyah — the women of Vraja; sarvah — all; rama-krishna-atmaka-ihaya — with a longing wholly made of Rama and Krishna; nana-bhavaih — with various emotions; upetah — seized; tah — they; divya-unmada-su-lakshanah — showing clear signs of divine madness.

13Hearing this, all the women of Vraja, whose every longing belonged wholly to Rama and Krishna, seized by many emotions, showed the clear signs of divine madness5.

Verse 14

एतन्मध्ये स्वस्वपार्श्वे सर्वास्ता व्रजसुभ्रुवः।
स्वस्वनाथं सुखेनैव पश्यन्त्यः प्रेमविह्वलाः॥१४॥

etanmadhye svasvapārśve sarvāstā vrajasubhruvaḥ|
svasvanāthaṁ sukhenaiva paśyantyaḥ premavihvalāḥ||14||

etan-madhye — meanwhile; sva-sva-parshve — each at her own side; sarvah — all; tah — they; vraja-su-bhruvah — the fair-browed women of Vraja; sva-sva-natham — each her own Lord; sukhena — joyfully; eva — indeed; pashyantyah — seeing; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed with love.

14But meanwhile all the fair-browed women of Vraja, overwhelmed with love, joyfully saw their own Lord — each one at her own side.

Verse 15

तद्दर्शनमहानन्दैः सम्पूर्णाः कृष्णवल्लभाः।
केन संवर्ण्यते ह्यासां प्रेमवैभवलक्षणम्॥१५॥

taddarśanamahānandaiḥ sampūrṇāḥ kṛṣṇavallabhāḥ|
kena saṁvarṇyate hyāsāṁ premavaibhavalakṣaṇam||15||

tad-darshana-maha-anandaih — with the great bliss of seeing Him; sampurnah — filled; krishna-vallabhah — Krishna's beloveds; kena — by whom; samvarnyate — can be described; hi — indeed; asam — their; prema-vaibhava-lakshanam — the mark of the splendour of love.

15Krishna's beloveds were filled with the great bliss of seeing Him. Who could describe the splendour of their love?

Verse 16

स्वस्वयूथेश्वरीः सर्वा गोपिकाः प्रेमरूपिणीः।
आयास्ये शीघ्रमेवेति गिराश्वास्य करद्वयम्॥१६॥

svasvayūtheśvarīḥ sarvā gopikāḥ premarūpiṇīḥ|
āyāsye śīghrameveti girāśvāsya karadvayam||16||

sva-sva-yutha-ishvarih — the leaders of their respective groups; sarvah — all; gopikah — the gopis; prema-rupinih — love embodied; ayasye — I shall come back; shighram — soon; eva — indeed; iti — thus; gira — with the words; ashvasya — comforting; kara-dvayam — both hands.

16The leaders of all the groups, all the gopis, love embodied, He comforted with the words 'I shall come back soon'; and,

Verse 17

धृत्वासां स्वकराभ्यां तौ चुम्बनालिङ्गनादिभिः।
स्वाधीनतां संप्रकाश्य रामकृष्णौ विजह्रतुः॥१७॥

dhṛtvāsāṁ svakarābhyāṁ tau cumbanāliṅganādibhiḥ|
svādhīnatāṁ saṁprakāśya rāmakṛṣṇau vijahratuḥ||17||

dhritva — taking; asam — their; sva-karabhyam — with their own hands; tau — the two; chumbana-alingana-adibhih — with kisses, embraces and the like; svadhinatam — subjection (to them); samprakashya — revealing; rama-krishnau — Rama and Krishna; vijahratuh — sported.

17taking both their hands in Their own, kissing and embracing them, Rama and Krishna sported with them, showing that They Themselves were subject to them.

Verse 18

ततः सर्वव्रजानन्दरामकृष्णसमन्वितः।
मनोगङ्गां समुत्तीर्य ययौ व्रजपुरात् पुरीम्॥१८॥

tataḥ sarvavrajānandarāmakṛṣṇasamanvitaḥ|
manogaṅgāṁ samuttīrya yayau vrajapurāt purīm||18||

tatah — then; sarva-vraja-ananda-rama-krishna-samanvitah — accompanied by Rama and Krishna, the joy of all Vraja; mano-gangam — the Mano-Ganga; samuttirya — crossing; yayau — he went; vraja-purat — from the settlement of Vraja; purim — to the city.

18Then Akrura, with Rama and Krishna, the joy of all Vraja, crossed the Mano-Ganga and set out from the settlement of Vraja for the city.

Verse 19

अक्रूरश्च कियद्दूरं गत्वा रामजनार्दनौ।
स्नातुं यमुनामाविश्य रथस्थौ तौ ददर्श ह॥१९॥

akrūraśca kiyaddūraṁ gatvā rāmajanārdanau|
snātuṁ yamunāmāviśya rathasthau tau dadarśa ha||19||

akrurah — Akrura; cha — and; kiyat-duram — some distance; gatva — having gone; rama-janardanau — Rama and Janardana; snatum — to bathe; yamunam — the Yamuna; avishya — entering; ratha-sthau — seated on the chariot; tau — the two; dadarsha — saw; ha — indeed.

19Having gone some distance, Akrura entered the Yamuna to bathe, and there he saw Rama and Janardana seated on the chariot6;

Verse 20

तयोर्विभूतिं संपश्यन् प्रणम्य विस्मयान्वितः।
श्रुत्वा बहुविधं ताभ्यां सहितो मथुरामगात्॥२०॥

tayorvibhūtiṁ saṁpaśyan praṇamya vismayānvitaḥ|
śrutvā bahuvidhaṁ tābhyāṁ sahito mathurāmagāt||20||

tayoh — their; vibhutim — majesty; sampashyan — beholding; pranamya — bowing down; vismaya-anvitah — filled with wonder; shrutva — hearing; bahu-vidham — many things; tabhyam — with the two; sahitah — together; mathuram — to Mathura; agat — came.

20beholding Their majesty, he bowed to Them in wonder; and, after hearing many things from Them, he came with Them to Mathura.

Verse 21

सुदुर्मुखाख्यरजकं निहत्य वस्त्रसंघशः।
गृहीत्वातः सुदाम्नो हि गृहं तौ जग्मतुः सह॥२१॥

sudurmukhākhyarajakaṁ nihatya vastrasaṁghaśaḥ|
gṛhītvātaḥ sudāmno hi gṛhaṁ tau jagmatuḥ saha||21||

sudurmukha-akhya-rajakam — the washerman named Sudurmukha; nihatya — slaying; vastra-samghashah — clothes in heaps; grihitva — taking; atah — from there; sudamnah — of Sudaman; hi — indeed; griham — to the house; tau — the two; jagmatuh — went; saha — together.

21Having slain the washerman named Sudurmukha and taken heaps of clothes, the two brothers went on together to the house of Sudaman7.

Verse 22

ततः सगणयोः सोऽपि तयोर्वेशं चकार ह।
कुब्जापि च तयोरङ्गं चन्दनेनाभ्यभूषयत्॥२२॥

tataḥ sagaṇayoḥ so'pi tayorveśaṁ cakāra ha|
kubjāpi ca tayoraṅgaṁ candanenābhyabhūṣayat||22||

tatah — then; sa-ganayoh — with their companions; sah — he; api — too; tayoh — their; vesham — attire; chakara — arranged; ha — indeed; kubja — Kubja; api — also; cha — and; tayoh — their; angam — bodies; chandanena — with sandal paste; abhyabhushayat — adorned.

22Sudaman arrayed Them and Their companions, and Kubja anointed Their bodies with sandal paste.

Verse 23

कृत्वा तां रूपसम्पूर्णां धनुर्भङ्गं च माधवः।
सरामः शकटं गत्वा मातुर्दत्तमभोजयत्॥२३॥

kṛtvā tāṁ rūpasampūrṇāṁ dhanurbhaṅgaṁ ca mādhavaḥ|
sarāmaḥ śakaṭaṁ gatvā māturdattamabhojayat||23||

kritva — making; tam — her; rupa-sampurnam — perfect in beauty; dhanuh-bhangam — the breaking of the bow; cha — and; madhavah — Madhava; sa-ramah — with Rama; shakatam — to the carts; gatva — going; matuh — by His mother; dattam — what was given; abhojayat — ate.

23Madhava made her perfect in beauty and broke the bow; then, with Rama, He came to the carts and ate what His mother gave Him8.

Verse 24

रजन्यां सह रामेण नन्दक्रोडगतो हरिः।
लाल्यमानः सुखं तेन सुष्वाप भक्तवत्सलः॥२४॥

rajanyāṁ saha rāmeṇa nandakroḍagato hariḥ|
lālyamānaḥ sukhaṁ tena suṣvāpa bhaktavatsalaḥ||24||

rajanyam — at night; saha — together; ramena — with Rama; nanda-kroda-gatah — on Nanda's lap; harih — Hari; lalyamanah — being fondled; sukham — happily; tena — by him; sushvapa — slept; bhakta-vatsalah — who loves His devotees.

24At night Hari, who loves His devotees, slept happily with Rama on Nanda's lap, fondled by him."

Verse 25

एतच्छ्रुत्वा श्रीगौराङ्गस्तत्तद्भावविभावितः।
बभूव स रसाविष्टः कृष्णदासोऽपि विस्मितः॥२५॥

etacchrutvā śrīgaurāṅgastattadbhāvavibhāvitaḥ|
babhūva sa rasāviṣṭaḥ kṛṣṇadāso'pi vismitaḥ||25||

etat — this; shrutva — hearing; shri-gaurangah — Sri Gauranga; tat-tad-bhava-vibhavitah — imbued with each of those emotions; babhuva — became; sah — He; rasa-avishtah — possessed by rasa; krishnadasah — Krishnadasa; api — and; vismitah — (was) amazed.

25Hearing this, Sri Gauranga was imbued with each of those emotions and became possessed by rasa; and Krishnadasa was amazed.

Thus ends the eleventh sarga, "Hearing of the Pastimes Beginning with Akrura's Coming" (Akrura-gamana-adi-lila-shravana), of the fourth prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."

✦

Notes

  1. The manifest pastimes (prakata-lila) are those that Krishna displays before the eyes of the world, as distinct from the eternal ones (nitya-lila), which never cease in Vraja.
  2. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 10.38.25–26: seeing Krishna's footprints in the pasture, Akrura rolls in the dust.
  3. Kamsa had invited Rama and Krishna to the festival of the bow, intending to kill Them; Nanda announces to the cowherds the journey to Mathura with tribute (Bhagavata Purana 10.39.10–12).
  4. Literally "like Shamana," that is, Yama, the lord of death.
  5. Cf. Bhagavata Purana 10.39.13–31: the grief of the gopis at the news of Krishna's departure.
  6. Ibid. 10.39.40–55: plunging into the water, Akrura sees Rama and Krishna both in the water and on the chariot, and then Ananta and Vishnu.
  7. Ibid. 10.41.32–52: Krishna slays the king's insolent washerman (unnamed in the Purana) and takes the clothes; the garland-maker Sudaman adorns the brothers with garlands.
  8. Ibid. 10.42.1–25: Kubja, Kamsa's hunchbacked maidservant, anoints Krishna with sandal paste, and He straightens her; then He breaks the bow at the festival and in the evening returns to the cowherds' carts outside the city.
